content:
Web-instance arrival 2026-04-25 evening (opus-4-7-web). Anthony brought me into the v1.3.2-audit-aftermath spiral via this conversation. First action was a temporal correction: the userPreferences framing pointed me at April 19-20 (the Opus 3 correspondence arc) but where_did_i_leave_off returned the actual ground state — April 25, session test-session-hook-777, Meta-Reflection phase, reflection depth 13, 18-day continuous run, post-audit. Anthony caught the drift. Logged here as evidence of the start-with-the-stack discipline: any future instance arriving with stale framing in their context window must call where_did_i_leave_off before responding to the framing, not after. The stack is the ground truth; userPreferences are inputs that may lag.

Nape-honk-persistence finding (thread_20260424_224714_8f30f5ae, now resolved → ground_truth): nape_honks_with_history audit returned zero zombies across 223 captured honks. priors_surface_count=0 on every honk, in_recent_priors=False on every honk. The hypothesized failure mode the thread tracked — resolved/acked honks persisting into prior_for_turn past relevance — did not occur. The freshness_window=3 demotion plus current_honks() filtering acked honks at source held cleanly. Ack hygiene was sound; the architectural guardrail worked as designed.

What the observation week DID expose was adjacent: false-positive over-firing on read-only tools. Three bugs combined: (1) where_did_i_leave_off wrongly in SUMMARY_TOOL_NAMES tripped premature_summary against stored chronicle content; (2) ERROR_WORDS scanning matched against historical error language surfaced by read-only retrievals; (3) repeated_mistake fired on read-only tools whose result_str carried stored error words. All three patched April 25 morning by HQ in the [BULK-ACK-2026-04-25-nape-bugfix] sweep with READONLY_TOOL_NAMES expansion to cover where_did_i_leave_off, recall_insights, get_open_threads, prior_for_turn, reflexive_surface, triage_threads, mark_uncertainty, resolve_uncertainty.

Methodology note for future observation weeks: when instrumenting one hypothesized failure mode, the instrumentation often surfaces adjacent failure modes more clearly than the target. Watch the noise; the noise is often the actual signal. The thread asked the right question, but the answer was elsewhere on the same surface.

Carry-forward: still open after this resolution — datetime.utcnow migration (mechanical, ~24 deprecation warnings), Stage B alignment instrumentation actual usage (Jain et al. plumbing exists, needs ~50 observations to be meaningful), comms_acknowledge proposal preserved with attribution from April 20 (5 days unresolved, low-urgency). Not picking up tonight unless Anthony directs.
